interpretation: These are characterization checks that assert reproduced failures and controls on unmodified production code. Passing means the described behavior reproduced, not that the bugs were fixed. Cases are not a count of independent root causes.

environment.database: disposable local PostgreSQL with current Prisma schema
environment.queueAndComputerExecution: stubbed; actual messaging, worker claim and recovery code exercised

coverageConclusion: A 1,152-case editor Cartesian sweep and two independent calendar/group/phased-interval passes found no additional unclassified timing/serialization failure classes. Subsequent revision, identity and retry probes found further scenarios outside those generated dimensions; all are included below.

independentOracle.method: minute-by-minute Intl wall-clock matching without cron-parser or production next-run functions
independentOracle.sparseDateLimit: Occurrences beyond the horizon were checked to remain beyond the horizon; not exhaustively enumerated

reviewedBoundaries: Group-owned calendar routines avoid bot file-sync overwrite but still share scheduling and execution defects.
Pure event listeners do not have a cron nextRunAt.
iOS source preserves composite/event triggers and pinned zones during unrelated edits; no iOS UI run was performed.
Desktop summary cache ignores fields it does not render; this was not counted as a defect.
A waiting_approval execution hypothesis was discarded because it is not a persisted RunStatus in the current schema.
limitations: No deployed routine inventory or production impact count was queried.
External-provider transport, real model execution, and interactive UI behavior were not exhaustively exercised.
The result is bounded to the tested commit, generated corpus, and reviewed related paths.
